output.subject: We have received your complaint about the paper statement fee
output.body:
Dear Customer,

Thank you for writing to us about your savings account. Please also thank ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧ for helping you write to us. We have received your complaint, and we want you to know that a person has read it carefully.

Here is what you told us. You have held your savings account with us for many years, since before the bank was called Meridian Harbor. This month a $2.00 charge described as PAPER STMT FEE appeared on your account. You told us nobody let you know about a fee for your statement. You mentioned that you do not use a computer and do not want to receive your statements that way. You asked us to remove the charge and not to charge it again.

We are looking into your complaint carefully. A specialist team is reviewing it, and we will respond within 10 business days. We're sorry to hear this has been a worry for you.

Thank you again for taking the time to write to us.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: The reply is written to the account holder (⟦NAME_1⟧) but greets them as 'Dear Customer'. Add their name to the greeting before sending.
⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧ is the granddaughter who typed the letter; the reply thanks her but is not addressed to her.
The reply says a specialist team is reviewing the complaint. Remove that sentence if you prefer not to mention any team.
Check whether the granddaughter is authorised to receive account information before sharing any specifics with her.
The account holder does not use a computer. Consider sending the reply, and any future response, by post.
Check whether and when the account holder was notified of the paper statement fee.
Decide on the request to refund the $2.00 fee.
Decide on the request to stop future paper statement fees, including any exemption that may apply to customers who cannot use electronic statements.
The account holder is 93 years old. Consider whether vulnerable-customer handling applies.
